adversary_breaks.expected: billing_destination_blocker must only bar verdicts that would grant the destination entitlement *via the transfer*. A provider-confirmed active verdict for D issued on D's own ticket (an INITIAL_PURCHASE / sync for D alone, not a TRANSFER side) is D's own purchase and must be applied; the held transfer has nothing to grant D and must not hold D's own paid entitlement hostage.
adversary_breaks.observed: persist_billing_verdict for D's OWN INITIAL_PURCHASE returns applied=false, withheld=true, billing.premium=false, transfer={state:'held', event_id:'w07-a5a-stale'}; complete_billing_webhook('w07-a5a-buy') raises 55000 'Webhook persistence is incomplete'; redelivery (fresh sync ticket, same active verdict) is withheld again; billing_entitlements row for D stays premium=false. Because S holds a lifetime product the blocker never lapses, so a paying user D never receives premium and RevenueCat keeps redelivering a 5xx-ing webhook until it gives up. VERIFIED (exit 3; 13 PASS / 3 BREAK in w07_03_attacks_head_run6.log).
adversary_breaks.repro: docker exec pickle-attack psql -U postgres -d attack -v w07_dsn="dbname=attack user=postgres password=pg host=127.0.0.1" -f /w07_03_attacks.sql  (section 'A5a held starvation (single destination)' in supabase/tests/w07_03_attacks.sql; DB = tests/shim_auth.sql + all migrations at 041d19a3). Scenario: S->D TRANSFER delivered after the device switched back to S; provider says S active (pickle_sensei_pro_lifetime, no expiry) and D inactive -> transfer 'held'. D then buys its own subscription: INITIAL_PURCHASE for D alone, begin_billing_verification([D]), persist_billing_verdict(D, ticket, active 30d), complete_billing_webhook.
adversary_breaks.title: A5a: held stale TRANSFER starves the destination's own independent purchase forever (INITIAL_PURCHASE never applies, webhook never completes)

adversary_breaks.expected: A destination side that has already been applied (settled) is no longer a barrier subject for that transfer. Later source verdicts (a new, unrelated purchase by the source) must not withhold the destination's own provider-confirmed renewal; the renewal must be applied and expires_at advanced.
adversary_breaks.observed: D1's renewal returns applied=false, withheld=true, transfer={state:'held', event_id:'w07-a5b'}; billing_transfer_recovery shows D1 side applied=true yet D1 is blocked because the source side is re-marked active (verified=true, active=true). D1's stored row keeps its OLD expires_at, so D1 will lapse at the old expiry although RevenueCat confirms the renewal. VERIFIED (same log).
adversary_breaks.repro: same command; section 'A5b applied destination re-barred'. Scenario: S->[D1,D2] TRANSFER; S confirmed inactive (source loss), D1 confirmed active and APPLIED through this transfer (destination side applied_at set), D2 never syncs so the transfer stays unsettled. S later buys a new subscription (persist_billing_verdict(S, own ticket, active)). Then D1's monthly renewal arrives: persist_billing_verdict(D1, own sync ticket, active +30d).
adversary_breaks.title: A5b: an already-applied transfer destination is re-barred when the source later buys a new subscription (legitimate renewal withheld)

adversary_breaks.expected: At minimum, a user's active verdict on their own ticket must be applied when the blocking transfer's source is itself confirmed active on its own account (that source is not losing anything - the transfer is stale). Never withhold entitlement from two mutually confirmed-active accounts simultaneously.
adversary_breaks.observed: Both verdicts return applied=false, withheld=true (S blocked by t2 where S is destination and D active; D blocked by t1 where D is destination and S active). billing_entitlements has no premium row for either; both transfers stay 'held' with sources active=true. Two paying users are locked out of premium until one of them lapses. VERIFIED (same log).
adversary_breaks.repro: same command; section 'A6 mutual hold'. Scenario: device switches S->D then D->S; two TRANSFER events w07-a6-t1 (S->D) and w07-a6-t2 (D->S) are queued; provider reports both S and D active (each has own purchases) on their own tickets: persist_billing_verdict(S, ticket, active) and persist_billing_verdict(D, ticket, active).
adversary_breaks.title: A6: mutual transfers (S->D and D->S both unsettled) leave BOTH provider-confirmed-active users non-premium with no recovery path except the other user's expiry

Also the candidate-owned security_regression.sql on BASE: exit 3, 'relation api_private.billing_transfers does not exist' (ac2_candidate_tests_on_base.log).

ATTACKS TRIED (all held on the candidate):
A1 barrier: destination verified first -> withheld, not premium, no entitlement row; complete_billing_webhook raises 55000 (retryable); billing_transfer_recovery lists it; source's confirmed loss releases destination; audit trail exact = [enqueued, destination_verified, destination_withheld, source_verified, destination_applied, confirmed]; webhook completes. FAILS ON BASE (this is the regress case).
A2 replay/duplicate submit: same withheld destination verdict persisted twice -> identical idempotent result, single destination_withheld audit row; divergent verdict on the sealed ticket -> 22023; inactive verdict on it -> 22023.
A3 crash between steps + lease expiry + redelivery: lease forced expired, redelivery re-claims, begin_billing_verification reuses the same durable transfer (1 transfer, 1 enqueued audit row), re-verifying the lost source keeps it lost, destination verdict on the new ticket applies, webhook completes.
A4 stale worker: a lapsed lease is refused (55000) by begin_billing_verification and enqueue_billing_transfer after a new worker took the delivery; fresh lease admitted.
A5 identity folding/cardinality/shape: duplicate + upper-cased ids fold, id on both sides dropped, malformed ids/ints/nulls ignored; all-both-sides and string-typed party fields -> outcome no_subjects (nothing queued, delivery not poisoned); exactly 16 parties admitted (16 sides), 17 -> 22023; wrong event.id, wrong event type, non-object payload -> 22023.
A6 clock boundaries: expiresAt 'infinity' -> 22023, malformed -> rejected, far-future finite (9999-12-31) stored; source premium=true with past expiry treated as inactive -> releases destination; source with entitlement expiring in 1.2s -> transfer 'held' and destination mirrors its own verdict; after expiry a destination sync confirms the transfer.
A7 unauthorised roles: anon/authenticated/service_role x {select/update/delete on billing_transfers, _sides, _audit; nextval on audit sequence; execute private helpers billing_transfer_party_ids/billing_destination_blocker/settle/reconcile/apply/note}, anon+authenticated on public enqueue_billing_transfer/billing_transfer_recovery, and authenticated with a destination JWT sub -> all 42501; service_role RPC path allowed.
A8 corrupt/partial persisted state: after destination verdict, webhook_events + billing_webhook_claims + tickets deleted -> billing_transfer_recovery still exposes the pending transfer; redelivery reclaims the same transfer, source loss releases destination, webhook completes.
A9 interleaved account switch A->B->C: B (destination of T1, source of T2) and C; with provider-confirmed losses only C is premium, both transfers confirmed, recovery empty.
A10 conflicting payload for same event id (permuted sources): claim and enqueue -> 22023; single transfer/enqueued row.
A11 two sources split + Auth deletion: one lost, one entitled -> held, destination mirrors own verdict; entitled source deleted from auth.users -> next destination reconciliation confirms.
A12 double admission under one lease: fresh tickets but 1 transfer, 2 sides, 1 enqueued row; first tickets settle and complete.
A13 concurrency (dblink, second session observed blocking on a row lock before first commits): (a) source then destination, (b) destination then source, (c) two destinations racing after source confirmed -> each applied once, one 'confirmed' audit row, (d) enqueue of S2->D racing the commit of S1's loss for S1->D -> T1 confirmed, T2 pending, D withheld by T2 until S2 confirmed. No deadlock, no duplicate transitions.
A14 destination deleted from Auth while withheld: no entitlement row fabricated, side marked user_missing_at, transfer confirms, verdict for missing user -> outcome user_missing; unrelated user's sync never withheld and has no recovery entries.
A15 stale-verdict resurrection via out-of-order tickets: newer inactive sync applied, older active TRANSFER ticket afterwards neither raises nor rewrites the side nor applies; source confirmation applies the newest (inactive) verdict, entitlement row keeps newest verification_order.

Observations (not breaks): (1) a source re-verified on a newer ticket reports applied=true because the row's verification_order/verified_at advance (pre-existing base semantics). (2) run_rls_tests.sh enumerates test files explicitly, so the new attack file is not picked up by the runner unless added there (not done: runner is outside attacker write scope). (3) INFERRED from code: complete_billing_webhook is unchanged by the candidate; its 55000 for a withheld destination relies on no entitlement row at >= the ticket's order, so a newer applied inactive sync lets the webhook complete while the (superseded) withheld verdict's transfer stays pending in recovery - consistent behaviour, not a defect.

A7 'clock boundaries' from the prior adversary suite reports BREAK by design conflict, not by accident: that probe expects a provider-confirmed *active* source to keep withholding the destination's own provider-confirmed active verdict (withheld=true, state=held). That expectation is the same mechanism that produced A5a/A6 (a still-entitled lifetime source starving the destination forever; mutual holds). Round 3 resolves it in favour of the prior-round 'expected' text for A5a/A6: once every source is provider-confirmed, the transfer parks as held and both accounts mirror their own provider verdicts, so the destination applies. The transfer stays held (visible in billing_transfer_recovery, re-settled on redelivery) and the source keeps exactly what the provider confirmed; the barrier still holds while any source is unverified. If the coordinator prefers the A7 expectation (hold until source expiry lapses), A5a/A6 cannot simultaneously hold for a lifetime source; a decision is needed. Independent regression coverage for held-source/expiry lapse in security_regression.sql covers the new semantics (W07-R2/W07-R3 blocks).

implement.summary: Defect on BASE_SHA (VERIFIED): no durable transfer queue exists. supabase/functions/api/index.ts handles RevenueCat TRANSFER events through the generic begin_billing_verification -> persist_billing_verdict -> complete_billing_webhook sequence (migration 20260907120000_billing_webhook_lease.sql defines these RPCs); there is no api_private.billing_transfers/_sides/_audit relation (BASE run of the new tests fails at security_regression.sql:5540 'relation "api_private.billing_transfers" does not exist'), so a destination's active verdict is applied as soon as it lands, with no barrier on the source's provider-confirmed loss and no append-only audit. Fix (forward migration 20260908150000_billing_recovery_transfer.sql, later than every existing migration; no applied migration edited): api_private.billing_transfers (state pending|held|confirmed, settled_at iff confirmed), api_private.billing_transfer_sides (source/destination per user, verdict+verification_order+applied_at+user_missing_at), api_private.billing_transfer_audit (identity id, enumerated actions); RLS enabled with zero policies and ALL privileges revoked from public/anon/authenticated/service_role; append-only triggers (row-level UPDATE/DELETE + statement-level TRUNCATE) refuse deleting or truncating any transfer history, mutating audit rows, reopening confirmed transfers, mutating applied sides or regressing verification order; public.enqueue_billing_transfer(event_id,payload,lease_token) and public.billing_transfer_recovery() are SECURITY DEFINER, search_path='', executable by service_role only, and enqueue requires the live webhook lease; private helpers (billing_destination_blocker(uuid), reconcile_billing_transfer_sources, settle_billing_transfer, apply_billing_transfer_side, note_billing_transfer, guard_billing_transfer_history) have EXECUTE revoked from all client and service roles. Wiring into the shipping path (behaviour, not an unused module): begin_billing_verification is replaced (same signature) to enqueue TRANSFER payloads (transferred_from/transferred_to app_user_ids, folded/deduped, 1..16 parties, replay idempotent, conflicting payload 22023) under the lease before issuing tickets; persist_billing_verdict is replaced (same signature) so the verdict is recorded on every open side for that user, the source loses as soon as its verdict lands, and a destination that is an unapplied destination of any open transfer whose source is still unverified (and present in Auth) is withheld (applied=false, withheld=true, billing.premium=false, no entitlement row, transfer={id,event_id,state}); complete_billing_webhook keeps raising 55000 while a ticket is withheld so RevenueCat redelivers; recovery/redelivery re-settles (a source missing from Auth is authoritatively absent). Barrier semantics resolved for the prior-round breaks: once every source of the transfer is provider-confirmed, both accounts mirror their own provider verdicts — a source the provider still reports entitled parks the transfer as 'held' (retains its entitlement, transfer stays visible in billing_transfer_recovery) but no longer withholds the destination's own provider-confirmed purchase/sync (A5a: INITIAL_PURCHASE applies, webhook completes, syncs keep applying); applied_at is not null destination sides are excluded from the blocker so a later source purchase re-parks the transfer as held without re-barring the applied destination's renewal (A5b: renewal applies, expires_at advances); mutual S->D / D->S transfers with both accounts confirmed active on their own tickets leave neither withheld (A6).
